key_insight: A monolayer graphene top contact can significantly improve AlInN/Si solar cell performance by boosting current collection and overall efficiency without changing open-circuit voltage much.
engineering_relevance: This suggests graphene is a practical low-temperature transparent conductive contact for enhancing nitride-based photovoltaic devices on silicon.
method: AlxIn1−xN solar cells were grown on p-type Si(100) with a thin a-Si buffer layer.
Three Al compositions were tested: x = 0.22, 0.35, and 0.43.
A monolayer graphene film was transferred onto the front surface as a semitransparent contact and compared with non-graphene devices.
evidence_signal: The devices were evaluated under illuminated and dark conditions, and graphene improved short-circuit current density, fill factor, and power conversion efficiency across all compositions.
watch_item: The transfer process must preserve graphene continuity and contact quality, since defects or poor interface coverage could limit repeatability and scalability.
paper_title: Enhancement of nitride-based solar cells using graphene as transparent contact layer
